title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The relevant objects are:
- The profinite completion of SL(2,Z) = <ρ,σ>, with ρ of order 6 (order 3 modulo ±1) and σ of order 4 with σ² = -1.
- Its quotient Γ̂_{0,3}-like group 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} = SL(2,Z)^/±1 = PSL(2,Z)^ = (Z/2 * Z/3)^.
- A larger group 𝔊' ⊃ 𝔊 corresponding to GL(2,Z)^ (Γ̂_{1,1} with orientation reversal). It contains an orientation-reversing element τ' with determinant character χ(τ') = -1, which conjugates σ to σ^{-1} = -σ.
- B_{ρ,σ}: a GT/Galois-type group of automorphisms u of the profinite group with multiplier μ = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ*. Each u sends ρ to a conjugate of a power of ρ and σ to a conjugate of a power of σ.
- The characters ε_3(μ) = (μ mod 3) ∈ {±1} and ε_2(μ) = (-1)^{(μ-1)/2}, i.e. μ mod 4. These are the signs needed because ρ^μ = ρ^{±1} (mod ±1) and σ^μ = σ^{±1} = ±σ.

The previous page builds a bijection M^eff_{ρ,σ}[0] ≅ S𝔊^eff_{ρ,σ}. It sends a triple (u,a,b) (u ∈ B, a ∈ normalizer of ρ, b ∈ centralizer of σ, with matching images in 𝒯 and Ẑ*) to (α,β,μ).

On this page:
- (63) For an arbitrary (u,a,b), the images satisfy u(ρ) = int(α)ρ, with α possibly orientation-reversing so that the conjugate is ρ^{ε'}, ε' = ε_ρ(α). They also satisfy u(σ) = ε·int(β)σ, the 𝔖-conjugate σ^ε with ε = ε_σ(β). However ε' need not equal ε_3(μ), nor ε equal ε_2(μ).
- Grothendieck therefore proposes a slightly bigger group than B_{ρ,σ}, in which B_{ρ,σ} has index 1, 2 or 4 (the two independent sign conditions). In 'good cases' this bigger group would be the group of rational points of a group scheme over Z.
- To kill the sign ε he replaces β by β' = τ'^ν β with (-1)^ν = ε (64). Then u(σ) = int(β')σ, i.e. [u,σ] = β'σβ'^{-1} (65).
- Consequently the elements of Γ̃_Q (the Galois/GT-type group), previously parametrized by (α,β) ∈ Π̂'_{0,3} × Π̂_{0,3}, are now parametrized by (α,β') ∈ Π̂_{0,3} × Π̂'_{0,3}. The two components satisfy the determinant/orientation constraints χ(α) = ε_3(μ) and χ(β') = ε_2(μ) (66).
- For the action on PSL(2,Z)^ = SL(2,Z)^/±1 the change is inessential, since -1 is killed. The formulas (67) remain u(ρ) = int(α)ρ, u(σ) = int(β)σ = int(β')σ, with the 'loop equation' αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1}ℓ_1^ν = β'σ(β')^{-1}ℓ_1^ν, where ν = (μ-1)/2.
- The next page notes that for SL(2,Z)^ itself (Γ̂^+_{1,1}) the new convention removes the sign ε from the loop equation.

Purpose: choose normalizations so that the profinite 'loop equation' describing the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) (or a GT-like group) on Γ̂_{1,1} ≅ SL(2,Z)^ / GL(2,Z)^ takes a sign-free form. The sign information is moved into orientation characters of the parameters α and β'.
errors: The relation in (67) is transcribed as 'αρ(α)σ′ = …'. From the image and the next page it should read αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1}ℓ_1^ν.
Minor ambiguity: in (64) the struck-out version wrote τ'^ν β'. The retained definition β' = τ'^ν β is consistent with (65)-(66).
No mathematical error is detected. The claim that B has index 1, 2 or 4 in the enlarged group is plausible given the two independent signs, but it is not proved here.

ideas.what: Profinite 'loop equation' (équation des lacets) for the GT/Galois action on SL(2,Z)^ / PSL(2,Z)^ via the elliptic generators ρ (order 3) and σ (order 4, σ² = -1), with multiplier μ and correction term ℓ_1^{(μ-1)/2}.
ideas.modern_name: GT-type relations for Γ̂_{1,1}; action of Gal(Q̄/Q) and GT on profinite SL2(Z) (genus-one Teichmüller tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara (GT); genus-one level work by Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto (1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the role of Γ_{1,1} and Γ_{0,4}. These explicit formulas are not published.

ideas.what: Normalization change β' = τ'^ν β, using the orientation-reversing element τ' of GL(2,Z)^, to absorb the sign ε_2(μ) into the orientation character of the parameter.
ideas.modern_name: Passing from SL2 to GL2 (orientation double cover / extended mapping class group) to absorb sign characters

ideas.what: An enlarged group containing B_{ρ,σ} with index 1, 2 or 4, conjectured in good cases to be the rational points of a group scheme over Z.
ideas.modern_name: unclear; possibly a pro-algebraic / group-scheme envelope of a GT-like automorphism group

missed.claim: Grothendieck suggests enlarging the GT-like group B_{ρ,σ} by the sign/orientation conditions, so that the result is (in good cases) the group of rational points of a group scheme over Z. This is not developed on this page.
missed.quote: Ceci suggère une définition d'un groupe un peu plus gros que B_{ρ,σ}, dans lequel B_{ρ,σ} serait comme sous-groupe d'indice 1, 2 ou 4 — et qui aurait l'avantage, dans les "bons cas", d'être le groupe des pts rationnels d'un schéma en groupes ... sur Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Giving GT-type groups for genus one an algebraic group-scheme structure over Z is not standard. Pro-unipotent/motivic versions exist, but an integral group-scheme model in this sense is not a standard notion. The remark is too sketchy to count as a result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mostly a bookkeeping/normalization step for the genus-one loop equation (SL2 vs GL2, absorbing signs). The fleeting remark about a group-scheme model over Z is mildly intriguing but undeveloped.
transcription_corrections: 'Ceci est lié à la convention qui me fait Γ_Q^~' should read roughly 'Ceci est lié à la convention que un [élément] de Γ̃_Q, que nous repérions par le couple (α,β) ∈ Π̂'_{0,3} × Π̂_{0,3}, sera désormais repéré par le couple (α,β') ∈ Π̂_{0,3} × Π̂'_{0,3}'.
'(qui se présente si (u,α,β) ∈ M_{ρ,σ}[0]^{tt})' is more likely '(qui se présente si (u,a,b) ∈ M_{ρ,σ}[0]^{eff})'.
The marginal '575' at top is a page reference. The archive page number shown is 545.
The word before 'sur Z' ('constructible') is uncertain. It is partially struck and illegible.
